subject: general
question: Ayushi bought a toy for ₹461, decorated it at a cost of ₹15, and sold the toy for ₹918. Find the loss or gain percentage.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Cost Price (CP) = 461 + 15 = 476.

Selling Price (SP) = 918.

Profit = 918 − 476 = 442.

Profit% = (442 ÷ 476) × 100.

Profit% = (221 ÷ 238) × 100 = (13 × 17 ÷ 14 × 17) × 100 = (13 ÷ 14) × 100 = 650/7%.

**∴ The correct answer is 650/7% profit.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Purchase Price = 461, Overhead Expenses = 15, Selling Price (SP) = 918.

**Formulas:** Total CP = Purchase Price + Overhead Expenses | Profit = SP − CP | Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c739860a267c11d79620403ed2baed5b55bbfad5efeaca2ba523097d8d1c26ca.png] 

⇒ Total Cost Price (CP) = 461 + 15 = 476

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = 918

⇒ Since SP > CP, it is a **Gain**.

⇒ Profit = 918 − 476 = 442

⇒ Profit% = (442 ÷ 476) × 100

⇒ Profit% = (13/14) × 100 = 650/7%

**∴ The correct answer is 650/7% profit.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Cost Price

The **Total Cost Price** includes the buying price plus any additional costs like **transportation, repairs, or decoration**.

Profit and Loss Condition

If **SP > CP**, there is a profit. If **CP > SP**, there is a loss. Percentage is always calculated on the **Total CP**.</p
